segments.source: Problem 506. The best route from Stone to Cedar
A road map can be modeled as a graph. The best route depends on the stated criterion, not on how short it looks on paper.
Stone–Dover–Cedar has segment costs [5, 6] (total 11); Stone–Oak–Meadow–Cedar has segment costs [4, 2, 5] (total 11); Stone–Linden–Cedar has segment costs [8, 3] (total 11).
A route is feasible only if all of its roads are open. The cost of a route is the sum of its segment costs. Choose the feasible route with the smallest total.
Which route should a traveler use from Stone to Cedar, and why?
1. List the candidate routes and their segment costs. 2. All listed routes are open. 3. Add the segment costs for every feasible route. 4. The smallest feasible total is 11, on Stone–Dover–Cedar.
A shortest path is a reasoning result: first respect constraints, then compare the remaining costs.
Weighted graph; delete forbidden edges; minimize the sum of edge weights.
